newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dec JGB soars to end near nine-month high. [CORRECTED 08:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Dec JGB soars to end near nine-month high. [CORRECTED 08:00 GMT]

text.p: The Key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract soared to end near a nine-month high in active trade on Tuesday.
(Corrects headline and first paragraph to read "nine-month high", not "six-month high") In the cash market, strong bids from end-investors set in to boost prices, traders said.

"The second wave of aggressive purchases drove up the JGBs. Investors, who once unloaded them to take profits after the first wave of market rises just after the BOJ's tankan survey (in late August), are now tapping the market with strong bids," said a bank trader.
December ended at 122.10, up from Friday's 121.20.
The December hit 122.14, the highest since December 13, 1995, when the key contract rose to 122.20.

"I just don't know how far the market will go. Everybody is waiting for a chance to buy-on-dips. But, in the current market, the longer they wait, the less opportunity they have to hunt the paper (JGBs)," said a brokerage trader.
Wednesday is the final trading day for cash bond delivery on September 30.
There is potential demand from investors who need to put more cash bonds into their portfolios before they close their half-year books on September 30.

Market sentiment was clearly bullish on receding fears of a supplementary budget after Friday's announcement of April-June gross domestic product (GDP) data. The government said that April-June GDP fell a real 0.7 percent from the previous quarter, or a drop of 2.9 percent on an annualised basis.

"We cannot immediately say we need more investment in public works just by looking at the (GDP) figures," Economic Planning Agency Minister Shusei Tanaka told a news conference on Tuesday. There was a holiday on Monday.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd JGB was at 2.835 percent in late afternoon, down sharply from 2.900 percent on Friday.

Meanwhile, some short position holders in the September JGB contract which expired on September 6 were said to be still unable to borrow the cheapest deliverable cash bonds for the period beyond September 30.
But some traders said the 161st JGBs' repo rate covering a period beyond the end of September hit a massive 30 percent in London trading last week. ---Yoshiko Mori, Tokyo Treasury Desk 813-3432-8676
